This update fixes download results, library records and saved Devil Cut projects, and makes the main controls easier to reach in smaller windows.

**Windows:** `Deviload-2.6.5-setup.exe`, or accept the update prompt in the app.

**Mac (test build):** accept the update prompt, or take `Deviload-2.6.5-macos-test.zip`, move it to Applications and run `xattr -cr /Applications/Deviload.app` once.

**Linux (x86_64):** `Deviload-2.6.5-amd64.deb` or `Deviload-2.6.5-x86_64.AppImage`; the AppImage updates itself.

What's new

- Saved projects retain their source records when the queue or library is cleared. New tasks no longer reuse deleted task IDs. Missing video sources can be located again without discarding the timeline.
- Playlist files have individual library entries and actions, including successfully downloaded files from a partially failed playlist. Repeated records of the same path do not inflate the library count. Download groups can be collapsed.
- The selected video container also applies to sources that already contain video and audio. Incompatible codecs are reported instead of silently returning another container.
- Download archives distinguish formats and destination settings. Skipped tasks say "Already downloaded" and offer "Download again" instead of reporting a new file that does not exist.
- Watched lists keep excess new entries eligible for the next check instead of marking them as downloaded.
- Link inspection and playlist selection use the selected cookies source. Retrying a failed task applies the current cookies settings. Instagram errors distinguish audience restrictions, an empty API response and request limits.
- Linux YouTube sign-in directs users to browser cookies or a cookies.txt file. Opening a browser alone does not transfer its session.
- Tray actions restore minimized windows, macOS handles reopening from the Dock, and signing out on macOS clears the site's cookies without clearing application storage.
- Small windows retain toolbar actions in a More menu. Settings are divided into categories, video/audio choices are separate from playlist/subtitle options, and the save-folder picker is available beside the format controls.
- Progress distinguishes merging, conversion, container changes and saving. Supporting buttons and idle mascot motion are quieter.
- Linux packages include media playback dependencies. AppImage startup isolates GIO modules from incompatible host plugins; CI checks startup on Debian 13 and Ubuntu 24.04.

- Mac and Linux: Deviload no longer looks through Downloads, Desktop and Documents at start for Deviload 1.x, which only ever ran on Windows; on Mac that search made the system ask for folder access every time

Thanks to Esquire_Gamer for testing on Mac.

Full changelog: https://github.com/Pronexsteam/deviload/compare/v2.6.4...v2.6.5
